Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a well-defined, thin-walled cystic lesion with an air-fluid level in the left lower lobe, which is a classic radiographic appearance of an infected intralobar pulmonary sequestration. This distinguishes it from tuberculosis (typically upper lobe), emphysema (diffuse hyperinflation without discrete fluid levels), or pulmonary edema (bilateral symmetric opacities).
